title: Add baseline-basin regression detector and traffic-affine fallback
author: Rohit Agarwal
release_notes: Add a new baseline-basin regression detector to the perf canary pipeline. Detector identifies persistent percentile 'basins' in latency distributions and triggers a traffic-affine fallback path that pins affected tenants to low-variance shards while rollouts are paused. Exposes metrics and alerts for basin detection and recovery. Configurable via feature flag and canary policy fields.
description: Motivation: We've seen recurring subtle regressions where a suite of percentiles (p50-p95) forms a sustained uplift 'basin' that is not caught by single-quantile detectors but degrades tail stability and increases cost. This change introduces a baseline-basin detector that looks for coherent multi-quantile uplifts sustained across cohorts and a traffic-affine fallback that isolates affected tenants to affinity shards to reduce cross-tenant noise while preserving capacity for healthy traffic. Design: detector computes a smoothed baseline per-tenant and per-route using an exponential window, then constructs a basin score from the weighted sum of relative percentile shifts (p50/p90/p95/p99) normalized by historical variance. A basin is signaled when score > threshold for N consecutive windows and corroborated by cohort consensus. The traffic-affine fallback uses a lightweight shard affinity mapping that routes flagged tenants to pre-warmed low-noise pools and reduces mixing with high-variance workloads. Feature flagging and rollout: gated behind redwood.perf.basin_detector and redwood.router.affinity_fallback; defaults disabled. Canary rollout plan: 1) unit/integration tests and local perf harness; 2) enable detector in perf-canary-only environment with synthetic injections; 3) staged rollout to 5% of canaries, monitor basin_detected and false-positive rates for 48h; 4) enable affinity fallback on 1% traffic for tenants with confirmed basins; 5) full rollout if FP < 1% and recovery metrics meet SLO. Observability and operator UX: new metrics added: perf.basin.score, perf.basin.detected{route,tenant}, perf.basin.duration_seconds, router.affinity.fallbacks_count. Dashboards and alert rule templates are included in docs/observability/basin-detector.md. API/Config: added canary policy fields basin_window_size, basin_persist_count, basin_threshold and router affinity_shard_count. Tested: unit tests for detector math, e2e in perf lab with injected 15% p90 uplift, benchmark script to reproduce basin shape, and audit logging. Backfill: migration includes a no-op config patch for Dedicated customers. Related work: follows ENG-2456 (perf signal fusion) and ENG-2479 (canary failover primitives).

review_comments: Aisha Khan: Nice approach. Can you add a short section in the docs explaining how basin differs from correlated tail regressions? Also please add metrics cardinality bounds for the per-tenant series.
Rohit Agarwal: Added docs section and limited the per-tenant metric tagset to route+tenant+region, added guidance in README.

Diego Marquez: Algorithm looks good but the thresholding feels brittle. Suggest exposing a sliding calibrator that adjusts baseline_threshold by traffic volume. Also add unit tests covering low-traffic edge cases.
Rohit Agarwal: Implemented volume-weighted threshold adjustment and added tests for <50-req windows. PTAL.
Lena Schultz: CI flaked in the early run due to a test relying on wall-clock timers; please use deterministic clock or table-driven fake clock (requested in review).
Rohit Agarwal: Replaced timers with fakeclock in canary tests; CI green on rerun. Marking as ready for merge.
Aisha Khan: Approving after confirming dashboards. One nit: document the rollback signal emitted to the console for on-call visibility.
Rohit Agarwal: Added rollout/README.md with on-call runbook and console signal explanation.
ci_log_summary: Initial CI: lint and unit passed, integration flaky due to real timers. Rerun after fixing fakeclock: full CI passed (unit/integration/e2e/perf). Benchmark harness run produced expected basin signature at injected 15% p90 uplift.
test_plan: Unit tests for basin math and boundary conditions; e2e in perf lab with synthetic uplift (scripts/perf/benchmark_basin.sh); staged canary rollout with observability checks; follow-on 72h monitoring for false positives and recovery stability.
post_merge_steps: Deploy feature flag off by default. Enable in perf-canary environment and run synthetic injection. If metrics stable, enable 5% of canaries; run 48h observation. Add migration note to Dedicated install notes. Backport to release/* if required.
notes_for_release: This introduces new config fields under canary policy and a router flag. No automatic behavior change when feature flags are off. Operators should add perf.basin.* to their dashboard and create alerts for perf.basin.detected with severity=page for production-critical routes.
risk_assessment: Medium. Detector is conservative and requires N consecutive windows to trigger; affinity fallback reduces blast radius. Main risk is false positives for low-volume tenants; mitigated with volume-weighted calibrator and safe defaults disabled behind feature flags.
